data.body:
INVESTIGATION (INTERMEDIATE, opus) — root cause:

CERTAIN/ACTIONABLE (A): runner.py:3384-3389 fail-closed print() omits _schema_result.errors. The violating field/value IS computed (and embedded in the synthetic finding description in /tmp/findings.json, which CI does not upload) but never reaches the job log → violation unrecoverable from CI evidence. Static-proven. TRIVIAL fix: append the schema errors to the fail-closed stderr message.

LIKELY-FUNCTIONAL (B, static-inferred): dispatch.py:1399-1505 frozen-field re-rejection — correction returns the payload only if all frozen fields (severity/category-canonical/description/file/cited_lines/finding_id) are byte-preserved; any LLM drift on a frozen field → attempt discarded → exhaustion → fail-closed. CANNOT be specified precisely without a captured malformed payload — fix (A) is the prerequisite that captures it.

Disproved: type/extra-property enum trap; corrector-is-blind (schema errors + schema rules ARE injected into the correction prompt). Confirmed: review.schema_correction_max_attempts configurable (code default=2, docstring=1 mismatch; clamp ceiling=3); raising it unlikely to help if the limit is structural.

Recommendation: land diagnosability fix (A) + reconcile the default mismatch now (TDD); track functional fix (B) as follow-up once (A) yields a captured payload. evidence_limits: specific PR#676 violation not determinable today (that IS the bug).
